# task_state_machine

Create a named-state CAESAR task backed by DCode runtime memory.

| Metadata | Value |
|---|---|
| Stable ID | `runtime.task_state_machine` |
| Origin | DCode |
| Category | Runtime Blocks |
| Family | Task |
| Monaco kind | `runtime_block` |
| Format | `task_state_machine <portal>/<name>:` |
| Valid contexts | `file` |
| Autocomplete | `task_state_machine tasks/name:<br>    states:<br>        idle<br>        running<br><br>    state idle:<br>        if target_state == states.running:<br>            transition running<br>` |

## Lifecycle

Activation declares states and task channels; the current handler runs while active and transitions only when script code requests one.

## Persistence

The state table and current state survive handler calls for the active runtime object.

## Runtime-memory fingerprinting

The activation source hash includes the script and template dependencies and is reported with loaded runtime memory.

## Runtime sections

- `states`
- `start`
- `state`
- `end`

## Generated channels

- `<portal>/<name>_running.value`
- `<portal>/<name>_target_frequency.value`
- `<portal>/<name>_actual_frequency.value`
- `<portal>/<name>_hold.value`
- `<portal>/<name>_current_state.value`
- `<portal>/<name>_target_state.value`

## Example

```lua
task_state_machine tasks/name:
    states:
        idle
        running

    state idle:
        if target_state == states.running:
            transition running
```
